方.meaning: A <part>sail</part> flaps on its mast, a dot of flag on top. Whichever way the wind blows, the sail swings round to show it, and the little boat follows. Sailors read it like an arrow: it tells them the <kanji>direction</kanji>.
方.on: A sailor sprays a garden <sound>ho</sound>se into the sail to push the boat the other way.
方.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of the waves and points the way with a <sound>ta</sound>co.

中.meaning: A <part>pole</part> skewers a <part>mouth</part> straight through, like a marshmallow on a stick. The mouth wriggles but can't slide off. The pole went in at the exact <kanji>middle</kanji>.
中.on: Stuck on the pole, the mouth just keeps <sound>chew</sound>ing gum, bigger bubble after bigger bubble.
中.kun: Lunch is a <sound>na</sound>an wrap with a whole <sound>ca</sound>rp stuffed in the middle.

事.meaning: At the top, a <part>one</part>-plank shelf over a <part>mouth</part>; below, a <part>rake</part> with a <part>crowbar</part> jammed straight through it. The mouth won't stop complaining about its broken rake. 'What's the <kanji>matter</kanji>?' you ask.
事.on: 'A <sound>jee</sound>p backed over my rake!' says the mouth. That's the matter.
事.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala climbs a <sound>to</sound>tem pole to see what all the fuss is about.

店.meaning: Rain drums on an open <part>shed</part> where a pushy trader sells umbrellas, using <part>fortune telling</part> on everyone who walks past: 'I see rain in your future!' It's already pouring. Everyone buys one, and the shed becomes the busiest <kanji>store</kanji> in town.
店.on: An opera <sound>ten</sound>or sings the prices from behind the counter.
店.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat runs the till, selling bags of <sound>se</sound>same seeds on the side.

内.meaning: Rain hammers down. A <part>person</part> dives under an open <part>frame</part>, pokes his head up through the top, and stays there, dry and smug. Everyone else is soaked; he's snug <kanji>inside</kanji>.
内.on: He stays in there all <sound>nigh</sound>t, listening to the rain drum on the frame.
内.kun: Inside, he finds a snack waiting for him: '<sound>Ooh</sound>, <sound>chee</sound>se!'

当.meaning: Step on the teeth of a <part>rake</part> and its handle swings up: whack, right on the nose! A <part>sparkle</part> of little stars spins above your head. Bullseye: a perfect <kanji>hit</kanji>.
当.on: Hopping about clutching your nose, you drop the rake on your <sound>toe</sound> as well.
当.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' you yell, as the handle hits you a second time.

右.meaning: A <part>slash</part> and a <part>one</part>-plank arm cross over a <part>mouth</part>, like a hand reaching down to feed it. You always eat with this hand, the one you write with: your <kanji>right</kanji>.
右.on: Your right hand twirls chopsticks through a big bowl of <sound>u</sound>don.
右.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat grabs the noodles with its right paw: '<sound>Gee</sound>, hot!'

曜.meaning: Every morning the <part>sun</part> comes up, and a <part>peacock</part> beside it fans out its two big feathers and squawks the name of the day: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday... It never squawks at the weekend. It only knows each <kanji>weekday</kanji>.
曜.on: The peacock flicks a <sound>yo</sound>-yo once for each weekday, then takes the weekend off.

火.meaning: Two sparks pop off either side, and in the middle a figure throws up its arms and flares out at the bottom like a dancer in a twirling skirt. It crackles, it spits, it's hot: <kanji>fire</kanji>.
火.on: A <sound>ca</sound>rp leaps out of the pond and spits water to put out the fire.
火.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>!' giggles the flame, as it tickles your marshmallow.

月.meaning: A tall window with two bars inside and a curved left leg leans against the night sky. Through it you watch the <part>moon</part> grow fat, then thin, then fat again. One full turn of that moon is one <kanji>month</kanji>.
月.on: A <sound>ge</sound>cko climbs up the moon's face, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
月.kun: The moon sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and drops a silver <sound>key</sound> into the sea.

前.meaning: Two <part>horns</part> sit on a <part>one</part>-plank bar like a hat. Under it, the <part>moon</part> and a <part>dagger</part> race each other. The dagger keeps stabbing at the moon's back, but the moon stays <kanji>in front</kanji>.
前.on: They race straight across a <sound>zen</sound> garden and wreck the raked sand.
前.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>!' calls the dagger, '<sound>eh</sound>, wait for me!' But the moon stays out front.

夕.meaning: Two slanted strokes and a dot: a thin crescent moon just rising. The sun has gone, the sky turns orange, and the dot is the first star coming out. Time to go home: it's <kanji>evening</kanji>.
夕.on: In the evening sky the crescent looks like a thin <sound>sec</sound>tor sliced from a pie.
夕.kun: <sound>You</sound> sit out on the porch in the evening and wave at the moon.

名.meaning: In the <part>evening</part> dark you can't see who's coming up the path. So a <part>mouth</part> calls out into the night, and a voice answers with one word: who they are. In the dark you only know them by their <kanji>name</kanji>.
名.on: Lost in a hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze at night, you shout your name until a friend finds you.
名.kun: Your friend holds up a warm <sound>na</sound>an with your name written on it.

二.meaning: Two planks stacked, the top one short and the bottom one long, like a bunk bed for sticks. The short stick sleeps on top, the long one underneath. Count the sleepers: <kanji>two</kanji>.
二.on: Both sticks are sewn to their bunks with a single sewing <sound>nee</sound>dle so they can't roll out.
二.kun: The two sticks share one <sound>fu</sound>ton and one <sound>ta</sound>co for breakfast.

発.meaning: A <part>tent</part> folds up its flaps, and under it <part>two</part> planks on a pair of <part>legs</part> start running. The whole campsite packs up and sprints for the bus. Time for <kanji>departure</kanji>!
発.on: The campers burst out of their <sound>huts</sound> before sunrise.
発.kun: Each camper grabs one <sound>ta</sound>co for the road, and the bus pulls out.

水.meaning: Drop a stone into a pond and this is the splash: a tall spout shooting up the middle, drops flying out to the left and right. Your shoes are soaked. It's <kanji>water</kanji>.
水.on: A wrapped <sound>swee</sound>t falls into the pond and fizzes in the water.
水.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat squirts water at a bee, which buzzes off with a short, cross '<sound>Zu</sound>!'

土.meaning: A post sticks up out of a long, flat field, a short crossbar nailed near its top. Pull it up and clumps of brown dirt cling to its bottom. Plant your seeds around it in the <kanji>soil</kanji>.
土.on: A <sound>do</sound>lphin flops onto the field and digs in the soil, very confused.
土.kun: The dust makes you sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', right in a sleeping <sound>chee</sound>tah's face.

場.meaning: On a patch of bare <part>soil</part>, <part>sunbeams</part> pour down through the clouds onto one bright spot. Here's where the picnic goes. Spread the blanket in the light and mark it: the perfect <kanji>location</kanji>.
場.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey hops in and claims the spot before anyone else.
場.kun: '<sound>Bah</sound>!' grumbles a man who wanted that very spot.

寸.meaning: A <part>golf club</part> swings down past a tiny ball. Missed by a hair! The golfer crouches and checks the gap with a ruler: exactly one thumb's width. He writes down the <kanji>measurement</kanji>.
寸.on: His caddie offers him a roll of <sound>su</sound>shi, but he's too busy measuring and only mutters '<sound>Nn</sound>.'

時.meaning: Every morning the <part>sun</part> clocks in at the <part>temple</part>, punching its card in the machine by the door. One day it oversleeps and rolls in at noon, still yawning. The head monk taps his watch: 'And what <kanji>time</kanji> do you call this?'
時.on: A <sound>jee</sound>p honks at the monk: 'Hurry up, your time is up!'
時.kun: On a <sound>to</sound>tem pole by the gate hangs a big brass <sound>key</sound> to wind the clock.

週.meaning: A runner does one <part>lap</part> of the track each day, then rolls down the <part>ramp</part> counting out loud: Monday, Tuesday... When she says Sunday she reaches the bottom: one whole <kanji>week</kanji>.
週.on: At the bottom the runner kicks off a <sound>shoe</sound>, one for each day of the week.

先.meaning: A mound of <part>soil</part> with a <part>slash</part> of weed sticking out of it grows a pair of <part>legs</part> and races everyone to the finish line. It always gets there first, long <kanji>before</kanji> the rest.
先.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try at the finish line salutes the muddy winner.
先.kun: It crosses the line ahead of a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a brass <sound>key</sound>, both still running.

地.meaning: A <part>scorpion</part> scuttles across the <part>soil</part> and digs in its tail. It burrows down and down until it hits solid rock: the hard <kanji>ground</kanji> under everything.
地.on: A <sound>chee</sound>tah sprints over the ground, and the scorpion pops back up to watch it pass.

士.meaning: Flip a mound of <part>soil</part> upside down and you get this: a wide brim on top, a short neat base below, a straight post in between. It tips its brim to everyone and holds every door. It's a <kanji>gentleman</kanji>.
士.on: He holds up a polished <sound>shi</sound>eld to keep the rain off strangers.
士.kun: He serves <sound>sa</sound>shimi, a cow says '<sound>Mu</sound>!', and he slices <sound>rye</sound> bread with his long sword.

売.meaning: A <part>gentleman</part> stands on a folded <part>blanket</part> draped over a pair of <part>legs</part>. His helper underneath walks him down the street while he shouts: 'Blankets! Warm blankets!' Everything must go. He wants to <kanji>sell</kanji>.
売.on: He sells the last blanket and buys a shiny <sound>bi</sound>ke with the money.
売.kun: '<sound>Ooh</sound>!' says a buyer, stroking the soft blanket.

会.meaning: Rain pours. Two strangers dash under the same <part>umbrella</part>, their <part>kite</part> strings tangled together below it. By the time they've untangled them and the rain stops, they've swapped names and phone numbers. A lucky <kanji>meeting</kanji>.
会.on: Then the wind snatches the umbrella, and it flies off like a <sound>ki</sound>te.
会.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, hello again!' they both say, when they bump into each other a week later.

休.meaning: A <part>coat hook</part> leans against a <part>tree</part>, tired of holding coats all day. It slides down the trunk, lies back in the roots and lets out a long sigh. Even a hook needs a <kanji>rest</kanji>.
休.on: A pool <sound>cue</sound> leans beside it, also taking a nap.
休.kun: '<sound>Yah</sound>!' the hook yawns, and curls up next to a bowl of <sound>su</sound>shi.

定.meaning: Under a <part>roof</part>, the family argues about dinner. Then a <part>giant boot</part> stamps down on the table: BOOM. Silence. The boot has decided, and nobody dares say no. It gets to <kanji>determine</kanji> everything.
定.on: Its choice is stuck to the fridge with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe: final.
定.kun: '<sound>Sa</sound>shimi for dinner, <sound>duh</sound>!' booms the boot, stamping once more.

母.meaning: Look through the kitchen <part>window</part>: a long bar of a counter runs straight across it, and two dots peek over the top, a pair of eyes that see everything. You can't sneak a cookie past them. It's <kanji>mother</kanji>.
母.on: She clips her <sound>bo</sound>nsai on the windowsill, still watching you.
母.kun: Mother sits in the kitchen with two <sound>ha</sound>rps, plucking one with each hand, then the other: <sound>ha</sound>rp, harp.

父.meaning: Two short strokes like raised eyebrows sit over two long strokes crossed like folded arms. Someone stands at the door, arms crossed, eyebrows up: you're late home again. It's <kanji>father</kanji>.
父.on: He fell asleep on the <sound>fu</sound>ton while waiting up for you.
父.kun: '<sound>Chee</sound>se! <sound>Chee</sound>se!' says father, snapping a photo of you sneaking in.
